exercises.statement: The independent auditor's report on Fenwick plc contains, after the "Basis for opinion" section, a section headed "Material uncertainty related to going concern". It refers to note 2, in which the directors explain that the renewal of the group's main credit facility, due in six months, has not yet been agreed. The "Opinion" section states that the financial statements give a true and fair view. What does this mean?
options: The auditor has issued a qualified opinion because of doubts about the company's survival.
The auditor considers the disclosure in note 2 adequate and draws users' attention to it, without modifying the opinion.
The auditor was unable to obtain sufficient evidence and therefore disclaims an opinion.
The auditor considers that the going concern basis of accounting is inappropriate and has issued an adverse opinion.
option_explanations: Incorrect: a qualification would follow only inadequate disclosure; the Opinion section still states a true and fair view.
Correct: under ISA 570, an adequately disclosed material uncertainty leads to an unmodified opinion with a separate going concern section.
Incorrect: nothing indicates a limitation of scope; the auditor did express an opinion.
Incorrect: an adverse opinion applies when the going concern basis is inappropriate, which is not the case here.
exercises.explanation: Option 2 is correct: under ISA 570, when the going concern basis is appropriate but a material uncertainty exists and is adequately disclosed, the auditor expresses an unmodified opinion and includes a separate section headed "Material uncertainty related to going concern" referring to the relevant note. Option 1 is wrong: a qualified opinion would be issued only if the disclosure were inadequate, whereas here the Opinion section still states that the financial statements give a true and fair view. Option 3 is wrong: nothing indicates a limitation of scope. Option 4 is wrong: an adverse opinion applies when the financial statements are prepared on a going concern basis although this basis is inappropriate, which is not the case here.
exercises.source_ref: ISA 570 (Revised) §22-23 (use of the going concern basis appropriate but a material uncertainty exists) — IAASB

exercises.statement: In an auditor's report on the financial statements of a listed company prepared under ISA 700 (Revised), the "Opinion" section comes first, followed by the "Basis for opinion" section.
exercises.justification: True: since the 2015 revision, ISA 700 requires the Opinion section to be presented first, immediately followed by the Basis for opinion section.
exercises.explanation: The revised auditor's report places the most important information first: the Opinion section (e.g. "give a true and fair view"), then the Basis for opinion (audit performed under ISAs, independence, sufficient appropriate evidence). Then come, where applicable, the going concern section, key audit matters, other information, the responsibilities of management and of the auditor, and other reporting responsibilities.
exercises.source_ref: ISA 700 (Revised) §23-28 (Opinion and Basis for opinion sections) — IAASB

exercises.statement: You are reading the auditor's report on a French listed group, a public-interest entity. Which of the following items must the report contain under article 10 of Regulation (EU) No 537/2014?
options: The fees billed by the auditor for each individual non-audit service provided to the group
An opinion on the effectiveness of internal control over financial reporting
A list of all the misstatements identified during the audit, whether corrected or not
The date of the auditor's appointment and the total uninterrupted engagement period, including renewals
option_explanations: Incorrect: fees are disclosed by the entity in the notes; the report gives no service-by-service fee breakdown.
Incorrect: an opinion on internal control over financial reporting is a US requirement (Sarbanes-Oxley, section 404(b)), not an EU one.
Incorrect: misstatements are communicated to management and those charged with governance, not listed in the public report.
Correct: article 10 requires the date of appointment and the total uninterrupted engagement period for public-interest entities.
exercises.explanation: Option 4 is correct: article 10 of the Regulation adds specific contents for public-interest entities, including the date of appointment and the period of total uninterrupted engagement, key audit matters, a statement that no prohibited non-audit services were provided and that the auditor remained independent, and confirmation that the opinion is consistent with the additional report to the audit committee. Option 1 is wrong: audit and non-audit fees are disclosed by the entity in the notes, not detailed service by service in the auditor's report (the report only has to indicate services provided in addition to the statutory audit that are not already disclosed in the management report or the financial statements, with no fee breakdown). Option 2 is wrong: an opinion on internal control over financial reporting is a US requirement (Sarbanes-Oxley Act, section 404(b)) for certain issuers, not an EU one. Option 3 is wrong: misstatements are communicated to management and those charged with governance (and summarised in the additional report to the audit committee), not listed in the public report.
exercises.source_ref: Regulation (EU) No 537/2014, art. 10(2), points (b), (c), (e), (f) and (g) (additional contents of the audit report for public-interest entities) and art. 11 (additional report to the audit committee)

exercises.statement: The auditor's report on Dunmore plc contains a "Key audit matters" section describing two matters: the impairment testing of goodwill and the recognition of revenue on long-term contracts. The opinion is unmodified. Which statement about this section is correct?
options: It gives a separate opinion on the goodwill balance and on contract revenue, in addition to the opinion on the financial statements as a whole.
It describes the matters of most significance in the audit, why each was significant and how it was addressed, without giving a separate opinion on them.
It lists the misstatements found by the auditor in these two areas that management refused to correct.
It replaces a qualified opinion: the auditor reports these disagreements here instead of modifying the opinion.
option_explanations: Incorrect: key audit matters are addressed in the context of the audit as a whole; no separate opinion is given on them.
Correct: ISA 701 requires describing the most significant matters, why they were significant and how they were addressed.
Incorrect: the section does not list misstatements; an uncorrected material misstatement would lead to a modified opinion.
Incorrect: ISA 701 states that a key audit matter is not a substitute for a modified opinion required by ISA 705.
exercises.explanation: Under ISA 701, key audit matters are the matters that, in the auditor's professional judgement, were of most significance in the audit of the current period; for each one the report explains why it was considered most significant and how it was addressed. They are addressed in the context of the audit of the financial statements as a whole, and the auditor does not provide a separate opinion on them, so option 2 is correct and option 1 is wrong. Option 3 is wrong: the section does not list misstatements; an uncorrected material misstatement would lead to a modified opinion. Option 4 is wrong: ISA 701 states that communicating a key audit matter is not a substitute for a modified opinion required by ISA 705.
exercises.source_ref: ISA 701 (IAASB) §8 (definition), §11 (no separate opinion), §13 (description of each key audit matter), §4 and §12 (not a substitute for a modified opinion) ; NEP 701

exercises.statement: The auditor of Kelso plc has concluded that the financial statements are free from material misstatement, but that the strategic report overstates the group's market share in a way that is materially misleading, and the directors refuse to correct it. Under ISA 720 (Revised), the auditor describes this uncorrected misstatement in the "Other information" section of the report, but the opinion on the financial statements is not modified on this ground.
exercises.justification: True: the opinion covers only the financial statements; an uncorrected material misstatement of the other information is described in the "Other information" section.
exercises.explanation: ISA 720 (Revised) requires the auditor to read the other information (here the strategic report) and to consider whether it is materially inconsistent with the financial statements or with the auditor's knowledge, or otherwise appears to be materially misstated. If management refuses to correct a material misstatement of the other information, the auditor communicates with those charged with governance and, in the report, includes in the "Other information" section a statement describing the uncorrected misstatement (§22(e)(ii)). Since the financial statements themselves are not misstated, there is no ground for a qualified or adverse opinion under ISA 705; in extreme cases the auditor may also consider withdrawing from the engagement where the law allows it.
exercises.source_ref: ISA 720 (Revised) (IAASB) §14-15 (reading the other information), §17-18 (response when a material misstatement exists) and §22(e) (reporting) ; NEP 9510

exercises.title: A qualified opinion at Ravensworth Group
exercises.context:
You are an analyst at an asset management firm. Ravensworth Group plc, a listed manufacturer reporting under IFRS, has just published its 2025 annual report. Its consolidated income statement shows a profit for the year of €72m; equity at 31 December 2025 is €410m. Extracts from the independent auditor's report:

"Qualified opinion. ... In our opinion, except for the effects of the matter described in the Basis for qualified opinion section of our report, the consolidated financial statements give a true and fair view of the state of the group's affairs as at 31 December 2025 and of its profit for the year then ended..."

"Basis for qualified opinion. The group's inventories are carried in the consolidated balance sheet at €64m. Management has not written down slow-moving inventories of the specialist components division to net realisable value, which constitutes a departure from IAS 2 Inventories. Had these inventories been written down, inventories would have been reduced by €16m, the income tax expense by €4m, and profit for the year and equity by €12m."

"Key audit matters. ... Impairment of goodwill (€220m). ... How our audit addressed the matter: we challenged the cash flow forecasts and the discount rate used by management..."

Answer your portfolio manager's questions in English.

sub_questions.prompt: What type of opinion has the auditor expressed, and why?
options: An unmodified opinion with an emphasis of matter, because the inventory issue is disclosed in the notes
An adverse opinion, because the misstatement is both material and pervasive
A qualified ("except for") opinion, because the misstatement is material but not pervasive
A disclaimer of opinion, because the auditor could not obtain sufficient appropriate evidence on inventories
option_explanations: Incorrect: an emphasis of matter never relates to a misstatement; here the auditor reports an uncorrected departure from IAS 2.
Incorrect: an adverse opinion requires pervasive effects; the misstatement is confined to inventories of one division and quantified.
Correct: the heading and the words "except for" show a qualified opinion: the misstatement is material but not pervasive (ISA 705 §7(a)).
Incorrect: a disclaimer relates to an inability to obtain evidence, whereas the auditor knows and quantifies the misstatement (€16m).
sub_questions.explanation: The heading "Qualified opinion" and the words "except for" show a qualified opinion. Under ISA 705 §7(a), it is expressed when misstatements are material but not pervasive: here the problem is confined to one balance (inventories of one division) and to quantified amounts. An adverse opinion (option 2) would require pervasive effects; a disclaimer (option 4) relates to an inability to obtain evidence, whereas here the auditor knows and quantifies the misstatement. An emphasis of matter (option 1) never relates to a misstatement.

sub_questions.prompt: Using the figures given in the Basis for qualified opinion section, calculate Ravensworth's profit for the year as it would have been if inventories had been written down in accordance with IAS 2, in €m.
sub_questions.explanation: Corrected profit = 72 − 16 (write-down to net realisable value) + 4 (reduction in income tax expense) = 72 − 12 = €60m. Deducting the gross write-down without its tax effect gives 56, a classic error; equity would likewise fall from 410 to 398.

sub_questions.prompt: Because goodwill impairment is described in the "Key audit matters" section, the auditor has expressed a second reservation, on the goodwill balance of €220m.
sub_questions.explanation: False: a key audit matter describes an area of significant audit attention and how it was addressed (ISA 701); it does not modify the opinion and gives no separate opinion. The only reservation in the report is the one described in the Basis for qualified opinion section (inventories).

sub_questions.prompt: In about 80 words, explain how the opinion would have differed (a) if the inventory misstatement had affected most of the balance sheet and the income statement, and (b) if the auditor had instead been unable to attend the inventory count and to obtain any other evidence on inventories.
sub_questions.model_answer: (a) If the misstatement had been pervasive, affecting many elements of the financial statements, the auditor would have expressed an adverse opinion, stating that the financial statements do not give a true and fair view. (b) An inability to obtain sufficient appropriate evidence is a limitation of scope, not a known misstatement: the auditor would have expressed a qualified opinion ("except for the possible effects") if the possible effects were material but not pervasive, or a disclaimer of opinion if they could be both material and pervasive.
key_points: Material and pervasive misstatement: adverse opinion (ISA 705 §8)
Inability to obtain evidence: scope limitation, judged on possible effects
Possible effects material but not pervasive: qualified opinion ("except for the possible effects")
Possible effects material and pervasive: disclaimer of opinion (ISA 705 §9)

exercises.explanation: The case reviews the ISA 705 grid: nature of the matter (misstatement or inability to obtain evidence) crossed with its effect (material only, or material and pervasive) gives qualified, adverse or disclaimer. The Basis for qualified opinion section quantifies the financial effects of the misstatement (ISA 705 §21), which lets an analyst restate profit and equity. Key audit matters never modify the opinion.
exercises.source_ref: ISA 705 (Revised) (IAASB) §7 (qualified opinion), §8 (adverse opinion), §9 (disclaimer) and §21 (quantification of the financial effects) ; ISA 701 §11, §12 and §15 ; IAS 2 §9 (lower of cost and net realisable value) — règlement UE 2023/1803 ; NEP 700
